newsitem.title: USA: Alaska wins $25 million in pipeline tariff case.
newsitem.headline: Alaska wins $25 million in pipeline tariff case.

text.p: Alaska has won about $25 million in a pipeline-tariff dispute over the Exxon Valdez oil spill disaster, the state's attorney general said Friday.

The U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia ruled that owners of the Trans Alaska Pipeline System (TAPS) may not use costs of the 1989 oil spill in their calculations of North Slope oil transportation tariffs, Attorney General Bruce Botelho said.

"This decision makes it clear that the oil companies cannot have an oil spill the size of the Exxon Valdez and then raise their tariffs so the citizens of Alaska have to pay for it," Botelho said in a news release.
At issue was about $100 million in additional TAPS tariffs claimed by Alyeska Pipeline Service Co., the consortium that operates the system.

The tariffs are the costs of running the 800-mile oil line and its Valdez marine terminal. Under Alaska's tax and royalty system, the state effectively pays a quarter of the TAPS tariffs through reduced oil revenues.
Botelho said Alyeska's owners had claimed that the Exxon Valdez oil spill was an event that should be considered a normal and ordinary part of operating the huge pipeline system.

The state prevailed in its argument that the 11 million gallon disaster, the worst U.S. oil spill, should be considered an extraordinary event, as defined by a 1985 TAPS tariff agreement, Botelho said.
The case was originally argued before the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. The U.S. Court of Appeals issued its decision on the years-old case last week, Botelho said.
The TAPS owners have yet to pay the $25 million, he said.
In an unrelated tariff dispute, the state and the oil carriers reached an agreement over how the TAPS owners' public relations and lobbying costs will be treated, Botelho said.
The result of the agreement was a $1.5 million payment to the state and a new set of rules, he said.
The dispute was over pipeline tariff calculations from 1993 to 1997, he said.
TAPS owners are British Petroleum, Atlantic Richfield, Exxon, Phillips Petroleum, Unocal, Mobil and Amerada Hess.
